skill.description: Use when the user asks to QA paid ad conversion tracking before launch or scale. It builds a pre-flight checklist, UTM rules, event specs, dedup checks, attribution-window notes, and modeled-gap flags.
skill.summary: Pre-flight QA for paid ad conversion tracking, UTMs, deduplication, and attribution-window alignment.

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown links, fenced prompt examples, inline-code formatting, and repository metadata URLs. No prompt-injection attempt, hidden command execution, runtime network call, or malicious exfiltration intent was found. One medium semantic issue remains: the optional memory save path uses a <topic> filename placeholder without an explicit sanitization rule.

remediation.issue: The optional memory save path includes a user-facing <topic> placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Require agents to slugify the topic to lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, and reject path separators before writing memory files.

semantic_findings.title: Unsanitized Memory Filename Placeholder
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to write results to memory/ad/conversion-signal-qa/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md after user approval. It does not explicitly require the topic segment to be slugified or stripped of path separators. A malicious or accidental topic value could cause writes outside the intended folder if the host agent uses it literally.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 67 contains a user-facing <topic> placeholder inside a write path, and no nearby instruction requires sanitization. The skill also requires user approval before writing, so the issue is a bounded path-handling risk rather than clear malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Paid campaigns can scale on broken conversion data when UTMs, events, and attribution windows drift. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a pre-flight QA, UTM spec, and launch-readiness report.
actual_capabilities: Builds a pass, fail, or needs-input tracking checklist from GA4 Conversions and Traffic-acquisition exports.
Defines UTM naming rules for source, medium, campaign, content, and term fields.
Creates a conversion-event spec with event names, value parameters, currencies, dedup IDs, and firing locations.
Checks manual test conversions for event name, value, currency, and source or medium consistency.
Flags cross-platform dedup gaps, attribution-window mismatch, offline import gaps, and iOS-ATT modeled data.
Routes unresolved scoring or reconciliation work to the appropriate paid measurement skill.
limitations: It does not score ROAS R1 or R2 veto items; the ad-account-auditor handles that decision.
It does not require direct Google Ads, Meta, tag manager, or pixel API access.
It needs user-provided exports and one manual test conversion to make evidence-based judgments.
It does not perform order-level incrementality or double-count reconciliation.

use_cases.title: Pre-launch Tracking QA
use_cases.description: Check events, UTMs, dedup IDs, attribution windows, and modeled-data gaps before a campaign goes live.

use_cases.title: Budget Scale Readiness
use_cases.description: Confirm that conversion data is trustworthy before a team increases spend across Google, Meta, or other paid channels.

use_cases.title: Client Measurement Standardization
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable UTM and event specification that agencies can apply across client accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Tracking QA
prompt_templates.prompt: QA my conversion tracking before launch. Platforms: [platforms]. Conversion actions: [purchase, lead, signup]. I will provide GA4 Conversions and Traffic-acquisition exports.

prompt_templates.title: Build UTM And Event Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a UTM scheme and conversion-event spec for this paid campaign. Include source, medium, campaign, content, term, event name, value, currency, dedup ID, and firing location.

prompt_templates.title: Find Measurement Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these GA4 exports and my manual test conversion. Mark each checklist item pass, fail, or needs-input, then list the exact fixes before I scale spend.

prompt_templates.title: Align Multi-Platform Attribution
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Google, Meta, and GA4 conversion evidence for dedup readiness, attribution-window alignment, offline import gaps, and iOS-ATT modeled data. Route anything that requires order-level reconciliation.

output_examples.input: Google and Meta campaign with GA4 exports and one test purchase.
output: Launch-readiness: fix first because Meta purchases lack a stable dedup ID.
UTM status: pass for source and medium, fail for mixed campaign casing.
Next action: add transaction_id to the purchase event and rerun the manual test conversion.

output_examples.input: New lead generation campaign without a final UTM scheme.
output: Recommended source values: google, meta, linkedin.
Recommended medium values: cpc, paid_social, display.
Lead event spec: generate_lead with lead_id as the dedup key and a stated attribution window per platform.

output_examples.input: Scaling review where platform totals differ from GA4 orders.
output: Dedup gate: needs-input because the single source of truth is not declared.
Attribution windows: fail because seven-day click and one-day view windows are compared as equal.
Handoff: route order-level matching and incrementality analysis to attribution-reconciler.

best_practices: Provide GA4 Conversions and Traffic-acquisition exports before asking for a launch-readiness decision.
Run one manual test conversion and record its event name, value, currency, and source or medium.
Choose canonical UTM values before campaign URLs are created.
anti_patterns: Passing checklist items without direct evidence from exports or a manual test conversion.
Mixing platform auto-tagging and manual UTMs without a documented rule.
Putting emails, names, order numbers, or other personal data into UTM fields.

faq.question: What data do I need to use this skill?
faq.answer: Provide the campaign platforms, conversion actions, GA4 Conversions export, GA4 Traffic-acquisition export, and one manual test conversion result.

faq.question: Does this skill access my ad accounts directly?
faq.answer: No. It works from user-provided exports and manual evidence. API access is optional through compatible host tooling.

faq.question: Can it fix broken tracking automatically?
faq.answer: It identifies the fix and writes a clear implementation spec. Your analytics or development team still applies changes in the real tools.

faq.question: Does iOS-ATT modeled data mean tracking failed?
faq.answer: No. Modeled or partial iOS data is treated as a flag. A complete lack of verifiable conversion evidence is a fail.

faq.question: When should I use the ad-account-auditor instead?
faq.answer: Use ad-account-auditor after the measurement plumbing is ready, when you need scored ROAS R1 and R2 decisions.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is structured for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and compatible agent-skill hosts.
